data.narrative:
Blue Energy, a growth-stage nuclear energy company founded by Jake Jurewicz, has raised $380M to date. The comparable universe for nuclear energy comprises 11 peers: 3 public companies (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private firms including Helion, Oklo, Valar Atomics, X-Energy, and Nano Nuclear Energy. However, the peer set lacks sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within the nuclear energy subsector to support a reliable peer-median multiple approach; only zero datapoints emerged from narrow stage and tier filtering despite six same-sector peers existing in the broader universe.

Consequently, valuation relies on the stage-progression method, which applies a 1.2x step-up multiplier typical of the Growth stage-to-next-stage transition. Applied to the $380M total raised as a proxy baseline, this yields an implied valuation of $456M. This method is the sole applicable triangulation technique given peer set constraints.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $388M to $524M, centered on a median of $456M. The median represents the only methodologically defensible point estimate. Key uncertainties include the absence of narrow-peer multiples to validate the stage progression assumption and the relatively sparse private-stage nuclear energy comparables at growth scale. Additional peer data or disclosure of recent market transactions in this sector would materially improve conviction in any specific valuation point.
